_readme: Shows attempted for a batch and dropped rather than force-fitted with weak/unclear/conflicting data. Checked against before picking future batch candidates so they are never silently re-attempted. 'reason' is 'sourcing_gap' (every fetchable filler/canon guide either 404'd, disagreed with AniList's own confirmed episode count, or returned unusable/wrong-show data), 'scope_mismatch' (doesn't fit this project's filler/canon premise at all regardless of sourcing, e.g. no preceding source manga), or 'out_of_scope' (a movie/theatrical release with no per-episode weekly-padding concept to speak of). Andreas reviews this list manually to hunt down better sources himself for sourcing_gap/scope_mismatch entries; out_of_scope entries are permanent exclusions, not something to revisit. Entries are removed once a show is actually loaded (see data/bootstrap/README.md's dated batch entries for the removal).

entries.title: Kinnikuman
entries.detail: No itemized filler/canon guide could be found at all. One animefillerlist.com fetch returned content for a completely different show (Fairy Tail OVAs), and no fandom wiki or aggregate search surfaced a real per-episode breakdown.

entries.title: Yashahime: Princess Half-Demon
entries.detail: Its manga is a LATER adaptation of the anime (started 2021, by a different author, after the anime aired) -- not a source the anime was adapted from. The reverse of every other show in this catalog. Doesn't fit this project's 'filler = anime content not adapted from a preceding manga' premise at all -- more research wouldn't resolve this, it's a structural scope question. Same treatment as previously-excluded original-anime shows (Code Geass, Evangelion, Samurai Champloo), which were never added to this list since they were filtered out before ever being attempted.

entries.title: Devilman
entries.detail: No itemized filler/canon guide exists anywhere for the original 1972 anime -- every filler-guide site's 'Devilman' results are actually for Devilman Crybaby (2018), a different, unrelated adaptation. Wikipedia's own episode list has no commentary distinguishing manga-adapted from anime-original content either. Conceptually murkier than a typical gap, too: the manga started barely a month before the anime and the two ran concurrently with different tones/audiences (the anime described as 'monster of the week' style) -- there may not be a clean episode-level canon/filler split to find even with better sourcing, unlike a normal case where the anime adapts a manga that already exists.

entries.title: Berserk: Ougon Jidai Hen

Structurally out of scope, not a sourcing gap — excluded from candidate picking, not something more research could resolve.
